# Feature request

<!--
The collection is a reference, so the bar for a new skill is not "it would be
useful" but "it is a distinct thing an agent can be wrong about". A skill that
overlaps an existing one splits the routing signal, and the agent picks the
wrong one some of the time.

Before writing a skill, read the two closest existing ones and say in your
issue how yours differs. If it does not differ, the answer is to strengthen
the existing one, and that is a perfectly good request too.
-->

## The gap

<!--
What can an agent get wrong today that this would prevent? "There should be a
skill about X" is not enough. Describe the failure, and the trigger that
should cause an agent to reach for the new skill.
-->

## Why the existing skills do not cover it

<!--
Name the closest existing skills and say what each of them leaves out. If you
have read them and believe one of them should simply be extended, say that
instead: extending is usually the better answer.
-->

## Where it would sit

<!--
Which domain or cluster in skills.sh.json, and what the routing sentence would
be. The routing sentence is the part that decides whether the skill is ever
loaded, and it has a hard budget: it competes for 8,000 characters with every
other description.
-->

## What it would cost

<!--
Roughly how many lines, and whether it needs supporting files. A skill that
needs a reference document is a different proposal from one that does not.
-->
